<HEAD>
<TITLE>EX-99.1</TITLE>
</HEAD>
<BODY bgcolor="#FFFFFF">
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif">

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 8%">
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 25pt"><IMG src="u10537u1053700.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.1</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto plc<BR>
2 Eastbourne Terrace<BR>
London W2 6LG<BR>
United Kingdom<BR>
T &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 2000<BR>
F &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 1800

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Press release
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Rio Tinto completes divestment of 61 per cent of Alcan Engineered Products</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>4 January&nbsp;2011</B>

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto has completed the divestment of 61 per cent of Alcan Engineered Products (AEP)
to certain investment funds affiliated with Apollo Global Management, LLC (Apollo) and the
Fonds Strat&#233;gique d&#146;Investissement (FSI). The terms of the transaction are confidential.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Apollo is now the majority shareholder in AEP with a 51 per cent stake in a new holding
company for AEP, with the FSI holding 10 per cent. Rio Tinto holds a 39 per cent stake.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Guy Elliott, chief financial officer, Rio Tinto, said: &#147;The closing of our majority
divestment in AEP marks Rio Tinto&#146;s exit of substantially all downstream businesses. Since
2008, we have completed divestments in excess of US$11&nbsp;billion.&#148;
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In 2009, Rio Tinto divested the Composites division of the Engineered Products business.
The Group maintains its ownership of Alcan Cable.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In 2010, Rio Tinto completed divestments of US$4.2&nbsp;billion comprising Alcan Packaging Food
Americas, Alcan Packaging global Pharmaceuticals, global Tobacco, Food Europe and Food Asia
divisions, Vickery (Coal &#038; Allied), Maules Creek (Coal &#038; Allied), Alcan Beauty Packaging,
Alcan Medical Flexibles and Cloud Peak Energy.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining Rio
Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed on
the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products
are aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals
(borax, titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are
strongly represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South
America, Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif">


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.2</B>
</DIV>

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 10%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><IMG src="u10537u1053700.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">

</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 88%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto plc<BR>
2 Eastbourne Terrace<BR>
London W2 6LG<BR>
United Kingdom<BR>
T &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 2000<BR>
F &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 1800

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Press release
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Rio Tinto&#146;s offer for Riversdale opens</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>11 January&nbsp;2011</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto has today sent its first Bidder&#146;s Statement to Riversdale Mining Limited (Riversdale)
shareholders in relation to the takeover bid for all the ordinary shares in Riversdale.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The offer is dated 11 January&nbsp;2011 and closes at 7.00pm (Sydney time) on 18 February&nbsp;2011, unless
extended or withdrawn.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">A copy of the Bidder&#146;s Statement was sent to the Australian Securities Exchange and is available at
<U>www.riotinto.com</U>.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining Rio Tinto plc,
a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed on the Australian
Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products are
aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals (borax, titanium
dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are strongly represented in
Australia and North America with significant businesses in South America, Asia, Europe and southern
Africa.
</DIV>


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont.../</I></B>
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 92%">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.3</B>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto plc <BR>
2 Eastbourne Terrace<BR>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Press release
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Completion of dispatch of Bidder&#146;s Statement</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>13 January&nbsp;2011</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto has today completed the dispatch of its Bidder&#146;s Statement and offers in relation
to the takeover bid by Rio Tinto Jersey Holdings 2010 Limited (RTJ)&nbsp;for all the ordinary
shares in Riversdale Mining Limited (Riversdale).
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">A copy of the notice of dispatch was sent to the Australian Securities Exchange and is
available at <U>www.riotinto.com</U>.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed on
the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products are
aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals (borax,
titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are strongly
represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South America,
Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont.../</I></B>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto Jersey Holdings 2010 Limited (ARBN 148 135 844) (a company incorporated in Jersey) (<B>RTJ</B>)
gives notice that its bidder&#146;s statement dated 10 January&nbsp;2011 and the offers made under its
off-market takeover bid for all of the ordinary shares in Riversdale have been sent as required by
item 6 of section 633(1) of the <I>Corporations Act 2001 </I>(Cth) (<B>Act</B>).
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The offers are dated 11 January&nbsp;2011.</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">A copy of the acceptance forms that accompanied the bidder&#146;s statement and offer is included with,
and forms part of, this notice in accordance with section 633(6) of the Act.

<HTML>
<HEAD>
<TITLE>EX-99.4</TITLE>
</HEAD>
<BODY bgcolor="#FFFFFF">
<!-- PAGEBREAK -->

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif">


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit 99.4</B>
</DIV>


<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 8%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10537u1053700.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 8pt">120 Collins Street<BR>
Melbourne 3000<BR>
Australia<BR>
T &#043;61 (0)&nbsp;3 9283 3333<BR>
F &#043;61 (0)&nbsp;3 9283 3707

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Press release
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Fourth quarter 2010 operations review</B>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>18 January&nbsp;2011</B>

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Chief executive Tom Albanese said: &#147;Running our operations at full capacity was a priority for Rio
Tinto in 2010, in an environment of strong prices for most of our commodities. Our success is
clearly demonstrated in iron ore where we set new quarterly and annual production records. During
the quarter we approved a further $5.5&nbsp;billion in value-adding growth projects, including the
expansion of our Pilbara iron ore operations to 283&nbsp;million tonnes a year and the first phase of an
aluminium smelting pilot plant in Quebec using our new AP60 technology.&#148;
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto&#146;s global iron ore operations set a new quarterly production record at 65&nbsp;million
tonnes (50&nbsp;million tonnes attributable) and a new annual record at 239&nbsp;million tonnes (185&nbsp;million
tonnes attributable).</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Mined and refined copper were down nine per cent and six per cent on the fourth quarter of 2009
and down 16 per cent and five per cent on full year 2009, in line with previous guidance.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Bauxite production increased nine per cent year on year in line with higher demand. Alumina and
aluminium production were broadly flat.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Australian hard coking coal production was up eight per cent on the fourth quarter of 2009 and
rose 20 per cent on full year 2009, following increased investment at the Queensland operations.
Australian thermal coal production was down nine per cent overall for the year, mainly due to wet
weather in the Hunter Valley.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>The force majeure declaration at the four Queensland coal mines remains in place. All the
Queensland coal mines are operational but are still constrained in some way by weather impacts,
including the impact on third party infrastructure. Rio Tinto is currently unable to provide an
estimate of the full impact of this adverse weather or the duration of the force majeure
declaration.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>On 8 December, Rio Tinto signed a new agreement with Ivanhoe Mines under which Rio Tinto will
assume direct management of the Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold project in Mongolia. The agreement also
gives Rio Tinto the right to increase its holding in Ivanhoe to 49 per cent.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>On 15 December, Rio Tinto completed the divestment of its remaining 48 per cent equity holding
in Cloud Peak Energy Inc. The total gross proceeds from the secondary offering of $573&nbsp;million were
received in December.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>On 23 December, Rio Tinto announced a A$16 per share cash offer to acquire all of the issued and
outstanding shares of Riversdale Mining Limited by way of a recommended off-market takeover offer.</TD>
</TR>

<TR>
    <TD style="font-size: 6pt">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR><TR valign="top" style="font-size: 10pt; color: #000000; background: transparent">
    <TD width="1%" nowrap align="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
    <TD width="1%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto approved major capital projects totalling $5.5&nbsp;billion during the fourth quarter,
bringing the full year total of project approvals to $10.8&nbsp;billion.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>
</DIV>

production, unless otherwise stated</I>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Pilbara marketing</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Sales volumes from the Pilbara region of Western Australia continued to set new records in response
to growing demand: fourth quarter sales of 58&nbsp;million tonnes were three per cent higher than the
corresponding quarter of 2009 and full year volumes increased nine per cent to 223&nbsp;million tonnes
(100 per cent basis).
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Pilbara operations</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Pilbara operations also set new quarterly and annual production records at 61&nbsp;million tonnes and
224&nbsp;million tonnes (100 per cent basis) as the mines operated at above nameplate capacity. The new
Hamersley mines, Brockman 4 and Western Turner Syncline, continued to ramp up whilst Robe River
benefited from rising production at Mesa A. In October Robe River reached a new milestone following
the export of its one billionth tonne of iron ore.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 3 December Rio Tinto Limited and Sinosteel Corporation announced the extension of their Channar
Mining joint venture in the Pilbara, leading the way for a further 50&nbsp;million tonnes of iron ore to
be produced over the next five years.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Important variations to the State Agreements were approved by the Western Australian parliament,
which will lead to greater operational flexibility for our Pilbara operations.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Pilbara expansion</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">During the fourth quarter, Rio Tinto announced investments of $4.3&nbsp;billion (Rio Tinto share $3.3
billion) for the Pilbara expansion to 283&nbsp;million tonnes per annum. Total Pilbara investment
approvals in 2010 were $7.2&nbsp;billion (Rio Tinto share $5.3&nbsp;billion).
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 20 October, Rio Tinto announced that it is to invest $3.1&nbsp;billion (Rio Tinto share $2.1&nbsp;billion)
in expanding its iron ore infrastructure capacity in the Pilbara to 283&nbsp;million tonnes per annum by
the end of 2013.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 1 December, Rio Tinto approved a further $1.2&nbsp;billion investment to lift its annual iron ore
production capacity in the Pilbara. The capital will be used for significant expansions at the
Brockman 4 and Western Turner Syncline mines. The third mine earmarked for expansion as part of
this programme, Nammuldi, is currently under study, with an investment decision expected in 2011.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s integrated operations will be progressively upgraded as follows:
</DIV>


<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt">
<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Iron Ore Company of Canada (IOC)</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Fourth quarter production of pellets and concentrate at IOC declined nine per cent on the same
quarter of 2009, reflecting lower mine equipment availability and severe winter weather conditions.
2010 saw a return to the normal proportions of concentrate and pellet sales in the overall sales
mix as demand levels recovered.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>HIsmelt</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In December the HIsmelt joint venture partners agreed to permanently close the Kwinana site and
terminate the joint venture. The majority of closure work is expected to be completed by 2014. The
technology business (100 per cent Rio Tinto owned) continues and a number of licensing
opportunities are progressing.

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Kennecott Utah Copper</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">As previously guided, lower ore grades accounted for much of the decrease in the annual production
of copper, gold and silver in concentrates. This was partly offset by record mill rates at the
Copperton concentrator. Molybdenum production rebounded in the full year in line with an increase
in ore grades
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Higher copper and molybdenum ore grades in the fourth quarter resulted in increased production of
metal in concentrate compared with the same quarter of 2009. Lower gold and silver ore grades led
to lower precious metal production in the fourth quarter compared with prior periods.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Refined copper production was marginally lower in 2010 due to a planned 19&nbsp;day maintenance shutdown
at the smelter, whilst refined gold and silver production benefited from processing higher grade
ore accessed in late 2009. Fourth quarter refined metal production declined due to lower
concentrate availability.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Escondida</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Fourth quarter contained copper mill production was 16 per cent lower than the same quarter of
2009, primarily due to declining grades and an eight day conveyor shutdown at the Laguna Seca
concentrator. Increased ore hardness and lower shovel availability at the mine led to further
decreases in copper concentrate production. This was partly offset by higher levels of recoverable
copper in ore stacked for leaching, resulting in an overall decrease in mined copper production of
11 per cent.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Fourth quarter refined copper production was broadly consistent with the previous quarter and the
same quarter of 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Grasberg</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Freeport is due to release its 100 per cent operating data for the fourth quarter on 20 January
2011. Rio Tinto&#146;s share of joint venture copper and gold in 2010 was impacted by the anticipated
lower ore grades and lower mill throughput; these factors reduced the Rio Tinto share of production
under the metal strip agreement.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Northparkes</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Mined copper production at Northparkes rose by 23 per cent compared with the same quarter of 2009
due to increasing production from the E48 block cave. Annual production increased by 14 per cent
compared with 2009 as a result of higher grade material mined and the ramp-up of the E48 block
cave.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Oyu Tolgoi</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 8 December, Rio Tinto announced that it is to manage the Oyu Tolgoi copper/gold project in
Mongolia under a new financial agreement with Ivanhoe Mines. Rio Tinto subsequently increased its
interest in Ivanhoe to 40.5 per cent through an early, partial exercise of the Series&nbsp;B warrants
and the previously announced purchase of shares from Robert Friedland.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto has committed to fully participate in Ivanhoe&#146;s rights offering and, following the
closing of the rights offering in February&nbsp;2011, it expects to increase its interest in Ivanhoe to
42.3% through the previously announced acquisition of 10&nbsp;million Ivanhoe shares from Citibank.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto also secured the right to increase its ownership in Ivanhoe to 49 per cent.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Provisional pricing</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The effect of provisional pricing of copper sales is estimated to result in an increase in
underlying earnings of approximately $180&nbsp;million in the second half of 2010.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">At the end of 2010, the Group had an estimated 266&nbsp;million pounds of copper sales that were
provisionally priced at US 433 cents per pound. The final price of these sales will be determined
during the first half of 2011. This compared with 239&nbsp;million pounds of open shipments at 30 June
2010 provisionally priced at US 296 cents per pound.
</DIV>

</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Bauxite</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Fourth quarter bauxite production was six per cent lower than the same quarter of 2009 but was nine
per cent higher for the full year in line with rising third party demand.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Alumina</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Fourth quarter alumina production was stable compared with prior quarters. Annual production
increased three per cent on 2009 when production cutbacks were made, primarily at the Vaudreuil
refinery.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Aluminium</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Fourth quarter aluminium production was consistent with the same quarter of 2009 while full year
production was in line with 2009.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Production at Kitimat was reduced due to the closures of lines 7 and 8 in September in preparation
for the modernisation project.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Laterri&#232;re returned to full production at the end of September following a power outage in July
which forced the temporary closure of one of the plant&#146;s two potlines. The loss of metal production
during the partial shutdown was around 24,000 tonnes.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Other movements included higher production at NZAS following a transformer failure in 2008 which
impacted 2009 and a gradual return to full capacity at the operating UK smelters, partly offset by
the cessation of smelting activities at Anglesey.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>



<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always">&nbsp;</H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif">



<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 8%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10537u1053700.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO LOGO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">
<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD width="47%"></TD>
    <TD width="5%"></TD>
    <TD width="47%"></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Head -->
<!-- Begin Table Body -->
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top">&nbsp;</TD>
</TR>
<TR valign="bottom">
    <TD align="left" valign="top">Continues
</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD align="right" valign="top">Page 5 of 26</TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Low snow and rain levels in the Saguenay region of Quebec during the first half of 2010 led to
reduced power generation, resulting in the need to purchase additional power under a specially
negotiated power block from the state utility over a 12&nbsp;month period. The impact on EBITDA in the
second half of 2010 was approximately $60&nbsp;million and the full year impact was $117&nbsp;million.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 1 October, Rio Tinto announced an investment of $140&nbsp;million in a leading-edge casting facility
to produce value-added billet at its aluminium smelter in Straumsvik, Iceland. This is in addition
to an investment of $347&nbsp;million to modernise and increase the smelter&#146;s capacity by 20 per cent
following the completion of a long-term energy supply agreement.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 14 December, Rio Tinto announced that it is to invest $758&nbsp;million on completing the first phase
of the AP60 plant in Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean, Quebec. An additional $300&nbsp;million will be invested
for further construction in preparation for the $2.5&nbsp;billion modernisation of the Kitimat smelter
in British Columbia.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 13 January&nbsp;2011, Rio Tinto gave notice of a force majeure event impacting the supply of
aluminium to some customers from its Boyne Smelter near Gladstone as a result of the severe
flooding across Queensland.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Hard coking coal production from the Queensland coal operations continued to benefit from the
recent investment in two additional shovels and two new truck fleets, although it declined by six
per cent compared with the third quarter following the heavy rainfall in December.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Semi-soft coal production was 20 per cent lower than the corresponding quarter of 2009, but 70 per
cent higher than the third quarter, primarily due to coal seam presentation in the mining sequence
relative to comparable periods. The thermal coal operations increased production by three per cent
compared with the same quarter of 2009. Blair Athol continued to wind down to 3&nbsp;million tonnes per
annum, partly offset by the ramp up of Clermont which produced 2.1&nbsp;million tonnes in the quarter.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 29 December, Rio Tinto declared force majeure on coal sales contracts from the Hail Creek,
Kestrel, Blair Athol and Clermont mines as a result of severe monsoonal rain in central and
northern Queensland. Limited operations are underway but Rio Tinto is currently unable to provide
an estimate of the full impact of this adverse weather or the duration of the force majeure
declaration.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The processing of lower grade ore from the Argyle open pit continued in the fourth quarter. Ore
processed increased 57 per cent in 2010, following the three month shutdown in 2009, but diamond
production was lower overall due to lower grades.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Diamond production at Diavik was 17 per cent higher than in 2009 reflecting a significant increase
in ore processed, partly offset by lower grades in the areas currently being mined. Operations were
scaled back in 2009 in response to the economic slowdown.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Minerals production in 2010 continued to demonstrate a healthy recovery in line with improving
global economic conditions. Fourth quarter borate production declined by 20 per cent compared with
the third quarter, due to adverse weather conditions in December in southern California and
scheduled plant shutdowns.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Titanium dioxide feedstocks production similarly mirrored an improvement in market conditions. The
21 per cent annual increase reflected an eight week summer shutdown at RTFT in 2009 and a full year
of mining in Madagascar, partly offset by the reduced shareholding in RBM following the BBBEE
transaction in December&nbsp;2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>OTHER CORPORATE ACTIVITY</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 18 October, Rio Tinto and BHP Billiton jointly ended plans for an iron ore production joint
venture in the Pilbara in Western Australia following extensive discussions with regulators.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On 4 January&nbsp;2011, Rio Tinto completed the divestment of 61 per cent of Alcan Engineered Products
to certain investment funds affiliated with Apollo Global Management, LLC (Apollo) and the Fonds
Strat&#233;gique d&#146;Investissement.
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>

</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>EXPLORATION AND EVALUATION</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Pre-tax and pre-divestment expenditure on exploration and evaluation charged to the profit and loss
account in 2010 was $589&nbsp;million compared with $514&nbsp;million in 2009. In 2010 the Group realised $86
million (pre-tax) from the divestment of central exploration properties, compared with $85&nbsp;million
in 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Exploration highlights</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">A non-binding Memorandum of Understanding was signed with Chinalco on 3 December&nbsp;2010 to establish
an exploration joint venture (JV)&nbsp;in China. The JV will explore mainland China for world-class
mineral deposits and is expected to come into operation in the first half of 2011. It is intended
that between three and five large area exploration projects will be selected for initial focus by
the JV, with the potential for additional regions to be added at a later date.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">At the Amargosa bauxite project in Brazil, the Order of Magnitude study continued and remains on
track for completion in the fourth quarter of 2011.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">A summary of activity for the period is as follows:

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining Rio Tinto plc,
a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed on the Australian
Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products are
aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals (borax, titanium
dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are strongly represented in
Australia and North America with significant businesses in South America, Asia, Europe and southern
Africa.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Production data notes</B>
</DIV>



<DIV align="left">
<DIV style="font-size: 1pt; margin-top: 6pt; width: 18%; border-top: 0px solid #000000">&nbsp;</DIV>
</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt">
<TR>
    <TD width="3%"></TD>
    <TD width="1%"></TD>
    <TD width="96%"></TD>
</TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(a)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Production of smelter grade alumina at Gardanne ceased at the end of 2008. Production
continues from the Gardanne specialty alumina plant.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(b)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto sold its 100% interest in the Brockville specialty alumina plant with an effective
date of 20 September&nbsp;2010. Production data are shown up to that date.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(c)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>The Beauharnois smelter ceased smelting operations in the second quarter of 2009. </TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(d)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>The
Anglesey smelter ceased smelting operations at the end of the third quarter of 2009.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(e)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Mine production figures for metals refer to the total quantity of metal produced in
concentrates, leach liquor or dor&#233; bullion irrespective of whether these products are then
refined onsite, except for the data for bauxite and iron ore which represent production of
marketable quantities of ore plus pellets.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(f)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto Alcan had an 80% interest in the Awaso mine but purchased the additional 20% of
production. Rio Tinto Alcan sold its interest in Ghana Bauxite Company, owner of the Awaso
mine, with an effective date of 1 February&nbsp;2010. Production data are shown up to that date.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(g)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto has a 22.95% shareholding in the Sangaredi mine but receives 45.0% of production
under the partnership agreement.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(h)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Thermal coal and semi-soft coking coal were previously reported under &#145;Other Coal&#146;.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(i)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Production commenced at Clermont in the second quarter of 2010.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(j)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>As a result of the initial public offering of Cloud Peak Energy Inc. on 20 November&nbsp;2009, Rio
Tinto held a 48.3% interest in the Antelope, Cordero Rojo and Spring Creek mines and a 24.1%
interest in the Decker mine. These interests were formerly reported under Rio Tinto Energy
America but are now managed by Cloud Peak Energy. Following a secondary public offering in
December&nbsp;2010, Rio Tinto completed the divestment of its entire interest in Cloud Peak Energy
Inc. with an effective date of 15 December&nbsp;2010. Production data are shown up to that date.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(k)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Through a joint venture agreement with Freeport-McMoRan Copper &#038; Gold (FCX), Rio Tinto is
entitled to 40% of additional material mined as a consequence of expansions and developments
of the Grasberg facilities since 1998. Rio Tinto&#146;s share of production reflects actual
production for the periods shown.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(l)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto sold its 100% interest in the Rawhide mine with an effective date of 25 June&nbsp;2010.
Production data are shown up to that date.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(m)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>Rio Tinto&#146;s share of production includes 100% of the production from the Eastern Range mine.
Under the terms of the joint venture agreement, Hamersley Iron manages the operation and is
obliged to purchase all mine production from the joint venture.</TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left">(n)</TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD>In March&nbsp;2009, Rio Tinto announced that HIsmelt would be placed on an extended care and
maintenance programme. In December&nbsp;2010, the HIsmelt joint venture partners agreed to close
the Kwinana site permanently and terminate the joint venture.</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><I>The Rio Tinto percentage interest shown above is at 31 December&nbsp;2010.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><I>Where Rio Tinto&#146;s beneficial interest in an operation has changed, as footnoted above, the share of
production has been calculated using the weighted average interest over the relevant periods. Rio
Tinto&#146;s interests in the Ningxia aluminium smelter, Corumb&#225; and Jacobs Ranch mines were sold in
2009. No data for these operations are included in the Share of Production table.</I>
</DIV>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left"><I>(a)</I></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><I>As a result of the initial public offering of Cloud Peak Energy Inc. on 20 November&nbsp;2009, Rio
Tinto held a 48.3% interest in the Antelope, Cordero Rojo and Spring Creek mines and a 24.1%
interest in the Decker mine. These interests were formerly reported under Rio Tinto Energy America
but are now managed by Cloud Peak Energy. Following a secondary public offering in December&nbsp;2010,
Rio Tinto completed the divestment of its entire interest in Cloud Peak Energy Inc. with an
effective date of 15 December&nbsp;2010. Production data are shown up to that date.</I></TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

October&nbsp;2009. Production data are shown up to that date.</I></TD>

    <TD><I>Through a joint venture agreement with Freeport-McMoRan Copper &#038; Gold (FCX), Rio Tinto is
entitled to 40% of additional material mined as a consequence of expansions and developments of the
Grasberg facilities since 1998. The 4Q 2010 results are not actuals but are forecasts from FCX&#146;s
most recent five-year plan and the full year 2010 results include the nine month 2010 actuals and
4Q 2010 forecasts. FCX is not releasing its actual 100% operating data for 4Q 2010 until the
release of its 2010 fourth quarter and full year results on 20 January&nbsp;2011.</I></TD>
</TR>

<TR style="font-size: 3pt"><TD>&nbsp;</TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD nowrap align="left"><I>(b)</I></TD>
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD><I>Net of smelter deductions.</I></TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>



<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Rio Tinto percentage interest shown above is at 31 December&nbsp;2010. The data represent full
production and sales on a 100% basis unless otherwise stated.</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Press release
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Rio Tinto Alcan&#146;s aluminium transportation returns to normal at Boyne Smelters Limited</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>21 January&nbsp;2011</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto Alcan today announced the termination of the force majeure event which had
affected some of its customers being supplied with aluminium from Boyne Smelters Limited
near Gladstone and that transport operations have returned to normal.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Flood waters are receding, road and rail access is available and the Port of Brisbane is
open, allowing the transport of products to domestic and international customers.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed on
the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products
are aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals
(borax, titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are
strongly represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South
America, Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont.../</I></B>
</DIV>

</DIV>
<BR clear="all"><BR>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Registered
in Australia Rio Tinto Limited 120 Collins Street Melbourne 3000
Australia ABN 96 004 458 404</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->

<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif">

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Exhibit&nbsp;99.6</B>
</DIV>

<P><DIV style="position: relative; float: left; width: 8%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><IMG src="u10537u1053700.gif" alt="(RIO TINTO)">
</DIV>

</DIV>
<DIV style="position: relative; float: right; width: 90%">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto plc<BR>
2 Eastbourne Terrace<BR>
London W2 6LG<BR>
United Kingdom<BR>
T &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 2000<BR>
F &#043;44 (0)&nbsp;20 7781 1800

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Press release
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Foreign Investment Review Board approval of Riversdale takeover</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>21 January&nbsp;2011</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto today received unconditional approval from the Australian Treasurer to acquire
up to 100 per cent of Riversdale Mining Limited.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Accordingly, as stated in the notice submitted to the Australian Securities Exchange
today, the condition to the takeover offer relating to this approval has been
fulfilled. A copy of this notice is available at <u>www.riotinto.com</u>.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The offer is scheduled to close at 7.00pm (Sydney time) on 18 February&nbsp;2011, unless
extended or withdrawn.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">For further information, please refer to the Bidder&#146;s Statement or contact the Offer
Information Line on 1800 102 639 (callers within Australia) or &#043;61 3 9415 4878 (callers
outside Australia).
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>About Rio Tinto</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto is a leading international mining group headquartered in the UK, combining
Rio Tinto plc, a London and NYSE listed company, and Rio Tinto Limited, which is listed on
the Australian Securities Exchange.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Rio Tinto&#146;s business is finding, mining, and processing mineral resources. Major products
are aluminium, copper, diamonds, energy (coal and uranium), gold, industrial minerals
(borax, titanium dioxide, salt, talc) and iron ore. Activities span the world but are
strongly represented in Australia and North America with significant businesses in South
America, Asia, Europe and southern Africa.
</DIV>


<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Cont.../</I></B>
</DIV>

</DIV>
